summary.qualitative: The candidate is structurally clean — all five sections in order, every section-D item carrying an explicit origin label (often with a secondary origin), no stray commentary — and its coverage of the narrative arc (bug-vs-by-design correction, "your call" delegation, gated execution, the post-baseline pivot, exchanges vs turns, cold-read targeting, ground truth from the ledger) is strong. It is materially weaker on numbers and mid-session engineering detail: it drops the 55,155 cache tokens/$0.576 cold-cell anatomy, the 22,585-char ≤400-char rubric sizing and multi-file-bullet rule, the 41% never-distilled figure, ~$0.002/session, the ~10x projection cut, 11 transcripts, 114 files, 2 commits, the git-identity convention, the NAST provenance of the headless recipe, and — notably — the disclosed ~/.claude-home `-r`/`--continue` trade-off and the transcript-parser iteration. Its grounding is mostly solid, but it invents two assistant errors that never happened (an assumption that config editing would fix home trust; a pre-baseline hypothesis that routing was the expensive step) and inverts two user-behavior readings, recasting the "is it installed / what does it do" questions and the "bug" framing as demonstrated expertise where the reference treats them as growth edges. Net: better than the reference on origin labelling discipline and failure-by-failure command detail, weaker on quantitative fidelity and honest characterization of user knowledge gaps.

candidate_claims.note: No such assumption appears in the transcript; the assistant inspected ~/.claude.json as evidence gathering and concluded from the start that flipping the JSON does nothing. Invented assistant error.
The transcript says the SKILL is a design guide, not an SDK; Jev is the model. Subject is swapped.

No such prior hypothesis is stated in the transcript — the assistant framed routing as a latency step to measure. The post-hoc finding (CLAUDE.md+SPINE floor is the cost) is grounded, the invented prior hypothesis is not.
The prompt is by-design behavior; the user calling it a "bug" is a mis-framing (a growth edge), not demonstrated expertise. Over-claimed.
The user asked what the skill does right after installing it, indicating unfamiliarity with Jev's primitives; candidate converts a knowledge gap into expertise.
The recall-over-precision preference was the assistant's proposal in turn 9, not something the user stated.

The recall rationale (Jev cheap, extractor costly, missing a correction costs the memory) is grounded, but tying it to the "live data is sacred" core value is the candidate's own inference, not stated in the transcript.
